BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p411/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p411/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p411/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas explains wazar as a refuge and cites poetry by Ṭābin al-Dathniya as Arabic evidence.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p411/r5.anchor: قال: الوزر الملجأ. قال: وهل كانت العرب تعرف ذلك

ITQAN:v2p378/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p378/r5.speaker: الضحاك
ITQAN:v2p378/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says lā wazar means there is no stratagem or escape, in Yemeni usage.
ITQAN:v2p378/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن الضحاك في قوله تعالى ﴿ لا وزر ﴾ قال لا حيل وهي بلغة أهل اليمن

ITQAN:v2p378/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p378/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v2p378/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says wazr means a grandchild in the Hudhayl dialect.
ITQAN:v2p378/r14.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال الوزر ولد الولد بلغة هذيل

ITQAN:v2p357/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p357/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p357/r9.claim: وزر means refuge or shelter; ʿAmr ibn Kulthum uses it in a line denying refuge.
ITQAN:v2p357/r9.anchor: لعمرك ما إن له صخرة لعمرك ما إن له من وزر

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r4.claim: Verses 7-15 answer demands to hasten Judgment: when upheaval arrives no one can flee except to God, and each must answer for every deed despite attempts to conceal it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r4.anchor: On that Day, there will be no resting place for anyone except with God.

FARRA:v3p210/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p210/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p210/r6.anchor: وقوله عز وجل: كلا لا وزر (11) . والوزر: الملجأ.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r5.claim: There is no shelter, fortification, or refuge; al-Suddi specifies there is no mountain to which people can flee when afraid.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p282/r5.anchor: {كلا لا وزر} لا حصن ولا حرز ولا ملجأ. وقال السدي: لا جبل

NAHHAS:v5p81/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p81/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p81/r2.claim: Al-maʾwā means refuge; wazīr may derive from entrusting affairs to a protector and relying on him, or from burdens carried, including precious metals.
NAHHAS:v5p81/r2.anchor: وهو الملجأ فقيل وزير مشتق من هذا لأن صاحبه قد سلم إليه أموره فلجأ إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r2.claim: The text leaves the arrival of Resurrection unstated, since the question about escape and the final return already imply that its terrors have come.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r2.anchor: وطوي التصريح بأن ذلك حلول يوم القيامة اكتفاء بذكر ما يدل عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r4.claim: The person asking where to flee is the disbeliever already mentioned in the surah, and the question expresses a wish for a place of escape.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r4.anchor: و { الإنسان } : هو المتحدث عنه من قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r6.claim: Kalla rebukes the hope of escape; a wazar is a refuge such as mountains or fortresses where one seeks protection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r6.anchor: ردع وإبطال لما تضمنه { أين المفر } من الطمع في أن يجد للفرار سبيلا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r7.claim: The clause denying any refuge may be God's answer, requiring a pause after ‘where to flee,’ or the person's own despairing answer, allowing the clauses to run together.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r7.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون { كلا لا وزر } كلاما مستأنفا من جانب الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r8.claim: On the alternative reading in which the person answers himself, he looks around and sees only Fire, as a hadith reports.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p345/r8.anchor: وذلك بأن نظر في جهاته فلم يجد إلا النار كما ورد في الحديث

JISHUMI:v10p7180/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7180/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7180/r8.claim: Wizr means a refuge such as a fortress; wazīr is related as a helper to whom one turns, and a wall is strengthened with a foundation.
JISHUMI:v10p7180/r8.anchor: والوزر: ملجأ من حصن أو غيره، ومنه: الوزير: المعين الذي يلجأ إليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p661/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p661/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p661/r5.claim: There is no refuge: every mountain or other place one might flee to is called a وزر.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p661/r5.anchor: { كلا } ردع عن طلب المفر { لا } لا ملجأ ، وكل ما التجأت إليه من جبل أو غيره

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r9.claim: لا وزر means there is no refuge from the Fire.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r9.anchor: أحدها : أي لا ملجأ من النار , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r10.claim: لا وزر means there is no fortress.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r10.anchor: الثاني : لا حصن , قاله ابن مسعود .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r11.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r11.claim: لا وزر means there is no mountain.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r12.speaker: ابن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r12.claim: لا وزر means there is no way to escape.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p153/r12.anchor: الرابع : لا محيص , قاله ابن جبير .

MUQATIL:75:8-18/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:75:8-18/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:75:8-18/r3.claim: Wazr is a mountain that protects a fugitive, and the word is also used for mountain in Himyari speech.
MUQATIL:75:8-18/r3.anchor: لا جبل يحرزك، ويسمى حمير الجبل وزر

TABATABAI:75:11-15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:11-15/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:11-15/r1.claim: The phrase no refuge rebukes the wish to flee; a wazr is a shelter such as a mountain or fortress, and the words are God's speech, not part of the person's plea.
TABATABAI:75:11-15/r1.anchor: والوزر الملجأ من جبل أو حصن أو غيرهما

TABRISI:75:12-14/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:12-14/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TABRISI:75:12-14/r1.claim: The preceding statement that there is no refuge means there is no fortress.
TABRISI:75:12-14/r1.anchor: وقيل: معناه لا حصن عن الضحاك

THALABI:v10p84/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p84/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p84/r11.claim: There will be no fortress, protection, or place of refuge; al-Suddi adds that even the mountain where people sought shelter will not protect them.
THALABI:v10p84/r11.anchor: كلا لا وزر لا حصن ولا حرز ولا ملجأ، قال السدي: لا جبل، وكانوا إذا فزعوا نحوا إلى الجبل

ELMALILI:75:1-30#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#3/r7.claim: “Wazar” originally means a heavy, steep, fortified mountain, hence a place of refuge.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#3/r7.anchor: sarp ve muhkem dağ demektir. Böyle dağlar firârîlerin sığındıkları yerler olduğu

ELMALILI:75:1-30#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#3/r8.claim: Because fugitives shelter there, “wazar” extends to any refuge or protector, including a mountain, fortress, weapon, person, or shield.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#3/r8.anchor: gerek dağ, gerek kale, gerek silah, gerek insan ve sâire mutlaka melce’, sığınak, sığınacak yer

ELMALILI:75:1-30#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#3/r9.claim: The cited poem illustrates that a young man has no refuge from death or old age.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#3/r9.anchor: لَعَمْرُكَ مَا لِلْفَتَى مِنْ وَزَر مِنَ الْمَوْتِ يُدْرِكُهُ وَالْكِبَرُ

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:11/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:11/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:11/r1.claim: On the Resurrection, no refuge or destination exists except God's presence; everyone will gather before Him and be told all good and evil they did or failed to do.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:11/r1.anchor: O gün herkes Allah’ın huzurunda toplanacak ve dünyada yapıp ettikleri ve yapması gerektiği halde yapmadıkları iyi ve kötü ne varsa hepsi ona haber verilecektir

RAZI-FULL:v30p195/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p195/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p195/r1.claim: Kallā rebukes the demand to flee.
RAZI-FULL:v30p195/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : { كلا } وهو ردع عن طلب المفر

RAZI-FULL:v30p195/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p195/r2.speaker: المبرد والزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v30p195/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjāj say wazar originally meant an inaccessible mountain, then came to mean anything one seeks refuge in or uses for protection.
RAZI-FULL:v30p195/r2.anchor: قال المبرد والزجاج : أصل الوزر الجبل المنيع

RAZI-FULL:v30p195/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p195/r3.speaker: المبرد
RAZI-FULL:v30p195/r3.claim: Al-Mubarrad cites Kaʿb ibn Mālik’s verse, where the word wazar names the swords and spearpoints that serve as the people’s sole refuge.
RAZI-FULL:v30p195/r3.anchor: وأنشد المبرد قول كعب بن مالك : الناس آلت علينا فيك ليس لنا … إلا السيوف وأطراف القنا وزر

RAZI-FULL:v30p195/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p195/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p195/r4.claim: The verse means there is nothing in which one can take refuge from God’s command.
RAZI-FULL:v30p195/r4.anchor: ومعنى الآية أنه لا شيء يعتصم به من أمر الله

STUDYQURAN:75:10/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:10/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:75:10/r1.claim: For disbelievers, the Hour brings no escape or refuge, as several other passages also make clear.
STUDYQURAN:75:10/r1.anchor: One of several passages to make clear that for those who disbelieve there is no escape or refuge once the Hour comes

TAB-FULL:v23p487/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p487/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p487/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses wazār as a fortress or refuge.
TAB-FULL:v23p487/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {لا وزر} [القيامة: 11] يقول: لا حصن

TAB-FULL:v23p487/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p487/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p487/r2.claim: In another report, Qatāda says there is no mountain to flee to.
TAB-FULL:v23p487/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {لا وزر} [سورة: القيامة، آية رقم: 11] قال: لا جبل

TAB-FULL:v23p487/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p487/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v23p487/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr glosses the word as no fortress.
TAB-FULL:v23p487/r3.anchor: عن مولى للحسن، عن سعيد بن جبير

TAB-FULL:v23p487/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p487/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p487/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk also glosses it as no fortress.
TAB-FULL:v23p487/r4.anchor: عن أبي حجير، عن الضحاك، لا حصن

TAB-FULL:v23p487/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p487/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p487/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says wazār means mountain in the language of Himyar.
TAB-FULL:v23p487/r5.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {كلا لا وزر} [القيامة: 11] يعني: الجبل بلغة حمير

TAB-FULL:v23p487/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p487/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p487/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says there is no place to hide from the matter and no escape from it.
TAB-FULL:v23p487/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {كلا لا وزر} [القيامة: 11] قال: لا متغيب يتغيب فيه من ذلك الأمر

TABRISI:75:4-11/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:4-11/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:75:4-11/r18.claim: There is no refuge or shelter, such as a mountain or anything else in which they could take cover; the word is related to a minister one turns to for help.
TABRISI:75:4-11/r18.anchor: أي لا مهرب ولا ملجأ لهم يلجؤون إليه والوزر ما يتحصن به من جبل أو غيره

ITQAN:v2p406/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p406/r8.speaker: أبو القاسم
ITQAN:v2p406/r8.claim: Abū al-Qāsim says wizr means rope and refuge in Nabatean.
ITQAN:v2p406/r8.anchor: وزر قال أبو القاسم هو الحبل والملجأ بالنبطية

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p499#7/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p499#7/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p499#7/r1.claim: There is no refuge; the basic sense of wazar is a mountain or fortress where one can seek protection.

SAMIN-DURR:75:11/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:11/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:11/r1.claim: The author notes that the discussion of كلا has already occurred.
SAMIN-DURR:75:11/r1.anchor: قوله: { كلا لا وزر }: تقدم الكلام في " كلا "

SAMIN-DURR:75:11/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:11/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:11/r2.claim: لا has an omitted predicate: لا وزر له.
SAMIN-DURR:75:11/r2.anchor: وخبر " لا " محذوف أي لا وزر له

SAMIN-DURR:75:11/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:11/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:11/r3.claim: The clause may quote the human being and thus be accusative, or be God's independent declaration.
SAMIN-DURR:75:11/r3.anchor: وهل هذه الجملة محكية بقول الإنسان فتكون منصوبة المحل، أو هي مستأنفة إخبارا من الله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:75:11/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:11/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:11/r4.claim: وزر means refuge such as a fortress, mountain, or weapon; the poem says no shelter saves a youth from death and old age.
SAMIN-DURR:75:11/r4.anchor:
والوزر: الملجأ من حصن أو جبل أو سلاح. قال:
4412 لعمرك ما للفتى من وزر

ZAJJAJ:v5p252/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p252/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p252/r8.claim: Wazar originally means a mountain people take refuge in; by extension it means anything one seeks as shelter or escape.
ZAJJAJ:v5p252/r8.anchor: الوزر في كلام العرب الجبل الذي يلجأ إليه: هذا أصله، وكل ما التجأت إليه

ZAJJAJ:v5p252/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p252/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p252/r9.claim: There will be no fortress or place of escape for them.
ZAJJAJ:v5p252/r9.anchor: ثم أعلم تعالى أنه لا حرز لهم ولا محيص

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p412/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p412/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p412/r1.claim: The root conveys a heavy load, physically or as sin and anxiety; related Qur’anic forms include burdens, sins, and a minister who carries responsibility.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p412/r1.anchor: والدلالة المشتركة فيها جميعاً: ثقل العبء، حسياً مادياً في الأحمال والأعباءـ ومعنوياً في الإثم والذنب، وفي الوزير يحمل الهم والعبء.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p412/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p412/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p412/r2.claim: Interpreting wazr as refuge draws on the root’s sense of a shelter for someone burdened by hardship; Arabic also calls a mountain a wazr for its protective refuge.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p412/r2.anchor: فتفسير الوزر بالملجأ، ملحوظ فيه هذه الدلالة الأصلية للمادة، في الملاذ لمثقل بعبء مادي أو هم نفسي

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p412/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p412/r3.speaker: ابن السكيت
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p412/r3.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt lists refuge, escape, fortress, and stronghold as glosses, and cites an Anṣārī poet’s line using wazr for protection.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p412/r3.anchor: وأنشد فيه "ابن السكيت" في باب الاجتماع بالعداوة قول الشاعر الأنصاري:

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p413/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p413/r1.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p413/r1.claim: Al-Raghib defines al-wazar as a refuge sought in a mountain.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p413/r1.anchor: نظر إليه الراغب فقال: الوزر الملجأ الذي يلجأ إليه من الجبل:

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p413/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p413/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p413/r2.claim: In context, al-wazar means there is no escape or refuge from the terror of resurrection, as the next verse declares the final resting place is with the Lord.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p413/r2.anchor: وهو في الآية أقرب إلى المهرب والملاذ من هول القيامة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p208/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p208/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p208/r5.claim: As the fleeing person seeks somewhere to shelter, the answer is that there is no refuge; wazr means a shelter or place of refuge.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p208/r5.anchor: والوزَر: الملجأ، فلا ملجأ يفر إليه الإنسان ويحتمي به وإنما

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r1.claim: There is no refuge or place of settlement except with God; the one fleeing can turn only to Him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p209/r1.anchor: والفارُّ يطلب ملجأ يأوي إليه ويعتصم به ويطلب الاستقرار ولكن لا استقرار إلا إلى الله، فإليه وحده المستقر

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p71/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p71/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p71/r1.claim: The answer to “Whither to flee?” is that every path closes except refuge with God; towards Him is the destination that Day.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p71/r1.anchor: Except for seeking refuge with God

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p333#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p333#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p333#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ لا وزر ﴾ قال كلا لا جبل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p140/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140/r1.claim: Kalla rebukes the wish and request for an escape.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140/r1.anchor: ردع عن طلب المفر وتمنيه لا وزر لا ملجأ

ALUSI-FULL:v29p140/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140/r2.claim: Wazar means refuge; it first meant an impregnable mountain, a common Arab place of flight, then any refuge such as a fort, weapon, or person.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140/r2.anchor: لا ملجأ وأصله الجبل المنيع وقد كان مفرا في الغالب لفرار العرب واشتقاقه من الوزير وهو الثقل ثم شاع وصار حقيقة لكل ملجأمن جبل أو حصن أو سلاح أورجل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p140/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140/r3.claim: The cited verse says a youth has no helper or refuge from death and old age, illustrating the word’s use.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140/r3.anchor: لعمرك ما للفتى من وزير من الموت يدركه والكبر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r3.claim: Kalla la wazar may be God’s words to the person asking where to flee, or the person’s own self-correction after asking.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r3.anchor: وكلا لا وزر يحتمل أن يكون من كلامه تعالى يقال للقائل أين المفر يوم يقوله أو هو مقول اليوم على معنى ليرتدع عن طلب الفرار وتمنيه ذلك اليوم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r6.claim: Kalla may instead function as an opening particle meaning “indeed” or as an emphatic “truly.”
ALUSI-FULL:v29p140#2/r6.anchor: وجوز أن تكون كلا بمعنى ألا الأستفتاحية أو بمعنى حقا

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:9-12/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:9-12/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:9-12/r7.claim: Kallā rebukes the attempt to flee; there is no refuge.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:9-12/r7.anchor: ردع عن طلب المفر. { لا وزر } لا ملجأ

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:9-12/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:9-12/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:9-12/r8.claim: The word “refuge” is a metaphor drawn from a mountain stronghold; its derivation relates to burden.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:9-12/r8.anchor: مستعار من الحبل واشتقاقه من الوزر وهو الثقل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p245/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p245/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p245/r7.claim: “No refuge” means there is no shelter, protector, fortress, or place of escape.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p245/r7.anchor: أي ملجأ ومعتصم ولا حصن ولا التجاء واعتصام

BIQAI-FULL:v8p245/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p245/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p245/r8.claim: The person’s own recognition that escape is impossible after first asking the question makes the scene’s terror more vivid.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p245/r8.anchor: فقال معبرا بالأداة الجامعة لمجامع الردع

DURR-FULL:v8p345/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r1.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r1.claim: The poet Amr ibn Kulthum is cited for Arab usage of wazr as a refuge or shelter.
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r1.anchor: عمرو بن كلثوم وهو يقول: لعمرك ما إن له صخرة لعمرك ما إن له من وزر

DURR-FULL:v8p345/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r2.claim: Ibn Masud glosses wazr as a fortress.
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r2.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في قوله: {لا وزر} قال: لا حصن

DURR-FULL:v8p345/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr, ʿAtiyya, and Abu Qilaba give the same gloss: no fortress.
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير وعطية وأبي قلابة مثله

DURR-FULL:v8p345/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says Arabs used wazr/wazīr for a mountain refuge in danger; the verse denies such shelter.
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r4.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله: {كلا لا وزر} قال: كانت العرب إذا نزل بهم الأمر الشديد قالوا: الوزر الوزير

DURR-FULL:v8p345/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r5.claim: Al-Hasan illustrates the usage with a herdsman surprised by cavalry and told to seek a mountain for refuge.
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r5.anchor: عن الحسن قال: كان الرجل يكون في ماشيته فتأتيه الخيل بغتة فيقول له صاحبه: الوزر الوزير

DURR-FULL:v8p345/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r6.claim: Mujahid glosses wazr as a mountain.
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {لا وزر} قال: لا جبل

DURR-FULL:v8p345/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r7.speaker: أبو قلابة
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r7.claim: Abu Qilaba says wazr means no cave, refuge, or shelter.
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r7.anchor: عن أبي قلابة {لا وزر} قال: لا غار لا ملجأ

DURR-FULL:v8p345/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r8.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak explains it as no protective mountain.
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r8.anchor: عن الضحاك {لا وزر} قال: لا جبل محرزة

DURR-FULL:v8p345/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r9.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak adds that wazr means mountain in the Himyari language.
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r9.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله: {لا وزر} قال: لا وزر يعني الجبل بلغة حمير

DURR-FULL:v8p345/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r10.speaker: مطرف
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r10.claim: Mutarrif glosses wazr as a mountain.
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r10.anchor: عن مطرف {لا وزر} قال: لا جبل

DURR-FULL:v8p345/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r11.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r11.claim: Qatadah says there is no mountain, fortress, refuge, or escape.
DURR-FULL:v8p345/r11.anchor: عن قتادة قال {لا وزر} قال: لا جبل ولا حرز ولا ملجأ ولا منجى

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3386#4/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3386#4/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3386#4/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd glosses wazara as a fortress: there is no fortress.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3386#4/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في قوله : لا وزر قال : لا حصن

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3386#4/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3386#4/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3386#4/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says wazara means fortress or refuge, so there is no fortress or refuge.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3386#4/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس في قوله : لا وزر قال : لا حصن ولا ملجا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420/r1.claim: Wazar means a refuge; the word originally means a mountain where one takes shelter.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p420/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى كلا لا وزر قال ابن قتيبة لا ملجأ وأصل الوزر الجبل الذي يمتنع فيه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#2/r2.anchor: ردع عن طلب المفر ﴿ لا وزر ﴾ لا ملجأ

BURHAN:v4p311/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p311/r11.speaker: ابن الحاجب
BURHAN:v4p311/r11.claim: Ibn al-Hajib says كلا requires preceding material to rebut according to the speaker's intent, whether the speech is quoted, narrated, or denied; he cites the fleeing-person and Moses episodes.
BURHAN:v4p311/r11.anchor: وقال ابن الحاجب شرطه أن يتقدم ما يرد بها ما في غرض المتكلم
